mutations.name: A refused manager instance restores the clean exit code
The --on refusal drops the identifier guidance and reverts to the mint's bare grammar sentence
mutations.find: console.error(c.red(`✗ ${(e as Error).message}. --on wants the manager INSTANCE id as \`cotal ps\` prints it (the \`manager <id>\` header in a multi-manager space, the \`instance <id>\` fact under \`cotal ps --wide\`), not the roster's principal id (\`local.U…\`, as \`cotal endpoints\` shows it)${principalClause}: \`${verb} --on <instance>\``));
mutations.expectRed: ps --on <roster principal id> is refused with the identifier --on wants and where ps prints it (#423)
mutations.cell: ps --on <roster principal id> is refused with the identifier --on wants and where ps prints it (#423)

why: The clean-exit-code mutation proves the partial-census cells actually watch the exit code, not just the message.
The --on-guidance mutation proves the new #423 cell actually watches the guidance text (the identifier and where ps prints it), not just the bare grammar phrase the mint already produced.
